title: Sync incident state transitions to Status Page draft updates (feature-flagged)
author: Devon Price
description:
Context: As part of Status Page Transparency Upgrades (ENG-4825), we want the public status page to track incident lifecycle more consistently and reduce manual work during transitions (Investigating -> Identified -> Monitoring -> Resolved). This PR adds a draft-sync integration: when an incident transitions state in incident-bot, we create/update a corresponding *draft* status page update with template-aware content and prefilled component selection hints. Drafts are not published automatically; a human still reviews/edits and hits publish.

What this does: (1) On incident state transitions, enqueue a StatusPageDraftSync job. (2) The job upserts a draft update for the incident’s external status page incident (creating the external incident if needed). (3) The draft is keyed by (incident_id, phase) so repeated transitions / retries are idempotent. (4) The draft includes: incident title, current phase, customer-impact summary (from existing classifier helper where available), and a required “next update by” timestamp carried over from the incident record. (5) A link back to the internal incident room + incident-bot permalink is embedded in the draft metadata for traceability.

Feature flag: gated by `STATUSPAGE_DRAFT_SYNC_ENABLED` (default false) and `STATUSPAGE_DRAFT_SYNC_REGIONS` (optional allowlist). This lets us canary in us-east first.

Rollback plan: Disable the flag(s) to stop syncing immediately (no restart required; dynamic config reload every 60s). No schema migrations. If we need to fully revert, a squash revert is safe because the integration is additive and does not change existing publish paths. Drafts created by this PR can remain; they do not affect customers unless published.

Operational notes: Adds rate-limit backoff + jitter and hard caps retries to avoid hammering the Statuspage API during flappy transitions. Emits metrics for job success/failure + latency and tags by phase and region.

Testing: Unit tests cover idempotency, phase mapping, and flag behavior. Integration tests use the mock statuspage client to validate payload shape and retry/backoff behavior.

Follow-ups: (a) Hook in the new phase-based copy blocks from PR #312 for richer templated drafts once merged everywhere. (b) Add UI affordance in Slack prompts to surface the generated draft link to oncall (tracked in ENG-4824).
commits: feat(sync): add StatuspageDraftSync job triggered on incident phase transitions
feat(statuspage): idempotent upsert of external incident + per-phase draft updates
feat(metrics): emit statuspage_draft_sync_* metrics with tags
test(sync): add unit/integration coverage for retry/backoff + payload mapping
docs(runbook): document canary + rollback procedure for oncall
review_conversation:
Miles Thornton (review): Idempotency looks good. One concern: what happens if the incident is created externally by Support before the bot sees the transition? Do we end up creating a duplicate external incident?

Devon Price (author): Good catch. The client now searches for an existing external incident by our stored external_id first; if absent, it also checks for a matching `metadata.internal_incident_id` (we set this on create). If neither exists, we create. If Support creates manually without metadata, we can’t reliably match; I added a note in the runbook: if Support must create manually, paste internal incident id into the external incident “internal refs” field so the bot can adopt it. We can tighten this later with a dedicated statuspage custom field once available.

Sara Al-Masri (review): Flag defaults to false — good. Can you make the dynamic reload interval configurable? Also, please ensure we don’t log the Statuspage API token on failures.

Devon Price (author): Updated: reload interval now comes from CONFIG_REFRESH_SECONDS (existing) and the new flags are read from the same source. Also sanitized error logging: we only log response status + request id; request headers are never logged.

Christine Wong (review): For draft content, can we ensure we don’t overcommit to a mitigation? The current text says “We are rolling back” in Identified if `mitigation.type=rollback`. That might not be accurate if we’re still deciding.

Devon Price (author): Agree. I changed the wording to conditional language (“We believe the issue is related to X; mitigation in progress (e.g., rollback)”). Also added a `mitigation.confidence` guard: only include explicit action if confidence is `high` (defaults to `unknown`).

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a hard guarantee that we never auto-publish. I see a `publish: false` field but want an assertion.

Devon Price (author): Added an invariant check in the Statuspage client wrapper: if any codepath attempts `publish=true` from this job it throws and increments a `statuspage_draft_sync_publish_guardrail` metric. Also added a unit test to cover it.

Miles Thornton (review): One more request: link the generated draft in the incident Slack channel so oncall can find it quickly.

Devon Price (author): I left that as a follow-up in ENG-4824 because it touches the Slack prompt flow and we’re mid-review on that PR. For now the draft link is in the incident-bot web UI and in the job logs; runbook calls that out.
deployment_notes: Canary plan: enable STATUSPAGE_DRAFT_SYNC_ENABLED=true and STATUSPAGE_DRAFT_SYNC_REGIONS=us-east on incident-bot in prod; monitor statuspage_draft_sync_success_rate and Statuspage API 429s for 48h; then expand to us-west and eu-west. Rollback: set STATUSPAGE_DRAFT_SYNC_ENABLED=false (dynamic config reload) to stop all new syncs; no impact to existing published status updates.
release_notes: Internal: incident-bot can now auto-create/update *draft* status page updates on incident state transitions (feature-flagged; no auto-publish).
